name: Cherry Canary
tagline: A chest wearable that tracks breathing, heart rate and oxygen to warn before levels become dangerous.
problem: Consumer devices alert only after blood oxygen has already dropped, the team says.
solution: An ESP32 wearable with pulse-oximetry and motion sensors streams to an app, and AI looks for early warning patterns.
demo_moment: Team-described: wear the device and watch live readings.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won “Best Social Good Hack - Bitcamp” among 223 submissions.
Targets leading rather than lagging indicators.

lessons: Argue why your signal arrives earlier than the incumbent's.
